messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Exporting samples.csv in RStan
parts:
Not sure what you mean by export. The doc for the sample_file in the stan() function says

A character string of file name for specifying where to write samples for all parameters and other saved quantities. If not provided, files are not created. When the folder specified is not writable, tempdir() is used. When there are multiple chains, an underscore and chain number are appended to the file name
There are thousands of functions in R even before you get into the optional R packages. If you just mean all the functions in rstan, you can do

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Exporting samples.csv in RStan
parts:
You need to pass in the inits as a function. So pass in
init_fun, where you define:

init_fun = function() {
return(list(alpha=alpha_init,
beta=beta_init));
}

- Bob

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Exporting samples.csv in RStan
parts:
On Sat, Oct 5, 2013 at 8:40 PM, Peter Li <li.pe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Also, do you know how I can specify inits in RStan? I tried setting inits equal to a list of all of the initial values that I wanted to use:

  radon_group_chr.sf1 <- sampling(radon_group_chr.sm, dataList.3, chains=1,init=dataList.4,sample_file=paste('radon_group_cp_',count,'.csv',sep=''))

 but I get the error:

Error in config_argss(chains = chains, iter = iter, warmup = warmup, thin = thin,  : 
  initial value list mismatchs number of chains
error specification of arguments; sampling not done

It needs to be a list, each element of which needs to be a list of all the initial values.  Suppose you have parameter alpha in your model, then the inits argument can be fed say for 4 chains as follows:

inits = list(c1=list(alpha=1), c2=list(alpha=2), c3=list(alpha=3), c4=list(alpha=4)).

So I think in your example, you should do init = list(dataList.4).

--
Jiqiang
